newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch union content with earlier BP refinery closure.
newsitem.headline: Dutch union content with earlier BP refinery closure.

text.p: The Dutch FNV Industriebond union said on Tuesday British Petroleum's decision to shut the Nerefco's Pernis refinery this year rather than next was acceptable and would not lead to any industrial action.

"We have an agreement with BP about this. We were in talks for nine months last year and we negotiated a good social plan," said Cees Kramer, the leader of the oil-refining division of the FNV Industriebond.

The Pernis refinery in Rotterdam, operated by BP/Texaco joint venture Nerefco, was due to close in 1998, probably in October. Despite expansion at Nerefco's other Rotterdam refinery, Europoort, over 300 jobs are to go.
Failure to reach agreement on the social plan in October led to wild cat action and talk of a strike.
BP announced earlier on Tuesday the plan to close Pernis earlier than expected.

"A decision was made to bring forward the date when crude processing would be discontinued at the Pernis refinery in Rotterdam. This will now take place by the end of this year," BP said in a statement in London.
Kramer said the closure was most likely to take place in November.
